title: Bytewell
tagline: A little code. A little wonder.
description: An original local-first BASIC workbench. Write a small program, draw with sixteen colors, step through it, and watch its variables change.
features: BAS import/export and browser draft saving

screenshots.alt: Bytewell desktop BASIC editor showing the Orbit study source, sixteen-color geometry output, and live scalar variables.

verificationEvidence: 32 interpreter tests, 29 real-browser UI regressions, JavaScript syntax check and static build passed on 2026-11-10. Native BAS download/reopen/run and 390px keyboard execution were verified through localhost. Exact scope and screenshots are recorded in docs/TESTING.md. Publication is handled by the repository GitHub Pages workflow; local QA evidence is retained here.
projectNotes: Independent learning project inspired by QuickBASIC 4.5. Not a DOS emulator, Microsoft product, or compatible QuickBASIC compiler.
Supports a documented scalar BASIC subset. No arrays, SUB/FUNCTION, file I/O, sound, or executable compilation.
